newsitem.title: JAPAN: FORECAST-Japan Feb c/a surplus to rise on weak yen.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Japan Feb c/a surplus to rise on weak yen.

text.p: Japan's current account surplus is likely to show a modest year-on-year rise in February, buoyed by an increase in the nation's trade surplus, economists said on Thursday.
The average of the economists' forecasts was for a current account surplus of 801.1 billion yen in February, up from a 750.0 billion yen surplus a year ago.
The economists' forecasts for the February surplus ranged from 710.6 billion yen to 860.0 billion yen.
The February current account figures are due to be released at 8.50 a.m. on Monday (2350 GMT Sunday).
"It (the current account) will show the same trend as the trade account," said Koji Shimamoto, an economist at the Industrial Bank of Japan (IBJ).
Japan's trade surplus rose for the first time in over two years in February. It climbed 6.5 percent from a year earlier to 686.72 billion yen, the first increase since November 1994.
The current account is a broader measure of trade including services as well as goods. The current account surplus rose in January for the first time in 17 months, reflecting the weaker yen.

Economists said the steady fall of the yen has accelerated Japan's exports while putting a brake on imports. The weaker yen has made Japanese products more competitive overseas, while boosting the price of imports into Japan.

Daiwa Bank Research Institute said the trade surplus was showing clear signs of growing in quantitative terms, and added that the current account surplus would follow suit. In quantitative terms, Japanese exports rose 7.6 percent in February from a year earlier while imports fell 2.7 percent, according to data already released.

Economists also said the yen's fall has been leading to a rise in the income surplus gained from Japanese investors' overseas investments and added that this will contribute to the overall current account surplus.
Forecasts by individual research firms are as follows:
DAIWA BANK RESEARCH 710.6 billion yen surplus
NCB RESEARCH INSTITUTE 801.0 billion yen surplus
INDUSTRIAL BANK OF JAPAN 850.0 billion yen surplus
